extracted.intended_audience: USPTO patent examiners and supervisory patent examiners (examining corps); patent prosecution practitioners as secondary audience
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for handling Requests for Continued Examination (RCEs) filed under 37 CFR 1.114: what makes an RCE proper or improper, eligibility requirements, how to treat submissions (entered or not), relevant time periods, and which form paragraphs to use in various procedural contexts (after final, after allowance, on appeal, after Board decision, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility for continued examination (general)
rubrics_metrics.description: To be eligible for continued examination under 37 CFR 1.114, the application must be a utility or plant application filed under 35 U.S.C. 111(a) on or after June 8, 1995, or an international application filed under 35 U.S.C. 363 on or after June 8, 1995 that complies with 35 U.S.C. 371. The RCE must be filed on or after May 29, 2000.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This eligibility requirement is repeated for multiple situations (after final, after allowance, on appeal, after Board decision, etc.) and must be checked before applying RCE procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required components of a submission under 37 CFR 1.114
rubrics_metrics.description: As set forth in 37 CFR 1.114, a submission may include an information disclosure statement, an amendment to the written description, claims, or drawings, new arguments, or new evidence in support of patentability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a reply to the Office action is outstanding the submission must meet the reply requirements of 37 CFR 1.111. The submission may also consist of arguments in a previously filed appeal brief or reply brief, or an incorporation of such arguments in the transmittal letter or other paper accompanying the RCE.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fee requirement for RCE
rubrics_metrics.description: An RCE must be accompanied by the fee set forth in 37 CFR 1.17(e).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the RCE lacks the required fee, the request is improper (see form paragraphs such as 7.42.10, 7.42.13, 7.42.16). If fee is missing but submission filed, the submission generally should not be entered; exceptions exist when amendment obviously places application in condition for allowance (with supervisory approval).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reply requirements when a reply is outstanding (37 CFR 1.111)
rubrics_metrics.description: If a reply to the Office action is outstanding the submission must meet the reply requirements of 37 CFR 1.111; otherwise use form paragraph 7.42.08 if the submission does not comply with 37 CFR 1.111.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Arguments previously submitted after final rejection may be considered a submission under 37 CFR 1.114 only if the arguments are responsive within the meaning of 37 CFR 1.111 to the outstanding Office action. Examiner should identify reasons why submission is not fully responsive in bracket 2 of form paragraph.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bona fide attempt to provide a complete reply (tolling effect)
rubrics_metrics.description: If reply to a final Office action is outstanding and the submission is not fully responsive to the final Office action, then it must be a bona fide attempt to provide a complete reply to the final Office action in order for the RCE to toll the period for reply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If not a bona fide attempt, treat the RCE as improper; prepare and mail 'Notice of Improper Request for Continued Examination (RCE),' Form PTO-2051. Examples of non-bona-fide submissions include IDS-only submissions or amendments that cancel all claims without presenting new or substitute claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-fully responsive submission — notice and shortened statutory period
rubrics_metrics.description: If the submission is a bona fide attempt but not fully responsive, applicant should be informed of the reasons why and given a new shortened statutory period of two months to complete the reply (see 37 CFR 1.135(c)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use form paragraph 7.42.08 to notify applicant and set the shortened period. The shortened period may be extended under 37 CFR 1.136(a) but in no case beyond the statutory maximum of six months (35 U.S.C. 133).

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-compliant amendment treated as proper RCE with Notice of Noncompliant Amendment
rubrics_metrics.description: An RCE filed with a submission that is an amendment not in compliance with 37 CFR 1.121 but that is a bona fide attempt to provide a complete reply should be treated as a proper RCE and a Notice of Noncompliant Amendment should be mailed to the applicant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant is given two months from the mailing date of the notice to provide an amendment complying with 37 CFR 1.121. See MPEP § 714.03 for amendment practice under 37 CFR 1.121.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presentation of claims for a different invention (switching inventions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants cannot file an RCE to obtain continued examination on the basis of claims that are independent and distinct from, or lack unity of invention with, the claims previously elected and examined as a matter of right (i.e., applicant cannot switch inventions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If RCE filed with an amendment canceling all claims drawn to the elected invention and presenting only claims to a nonelected invention, treat the RCE as proper but do not enter the amendment; give applicant two months to submit a complete reply. Use form paragraphs 8.04 or 8.26 as appropriate and refer to 37 CFR 1.145 and MPEP § 821.03.

rubrics_metrics.name: New matter prohibition (35 U.S.C. 132(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: 35 U.S.C. 132(a) provides that 'No amendment shall introduce new matter into the disclosure of the invention.' Any amendment entered pursuant to 37 CFR 1.114 that is determined to contain new matter should be treated as a reply under 37 CFR 1.111 determined to contain new matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If applicant seeks to add new matter, 37 CFR 1.114 procedure is not available; applicant must file a continuation-in-part under 37 CFR 1.53(b) containing such new matter. See MPEP §§ 608.04 - 608.04(c).

rubrics_metrics.name: Making first action after RCE final — conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: The action immediately subsequent to the filing of an RCE with a submission and fee under 37 CFR 1.114 may be made final only if the conditions set forth in MPEP § 706.07(b) are met.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It would not be proper to make final a first Office action immediately after the filing of an RCE if the first Office action includes a new ground of rejection. Use form paragraph 7.42.09 if appropriate to make the first action after filing the RCE final.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of RCE filed after allowance or Quayle action
rubrics_metrics.description: If an RCE, including the fee and a submission, is filed in an application that has been allowed, prosecution will be reopened. If the issue fee has been paid, payment of the fee for an RCE and a submission without a petition under 37 CFR 1.313 to withdraw the application from issue will not avoid issuance of the application as a patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If RCE filed after allowance but before payment of issue fee, a petition under 1.313 is not required. If RCE filed after issue fee paid and petition under 1.313 is filed and granted, prosecution will be reopened but applicant may not obtain a refund of the issue fee. Use form paragraph 7.42.05 to notify applicant that prosecution has been reopened and the submission entered.

rubrics_metrics.name: RCE filed after appeal but before Board decision — withdrawal of appeal
rubrics_metrics.description: If an applicant files an RCE under 37 CFR 1.114 after filing a Notice of Appeal to the Patent Trial and Appeal Board, but prior to a decision on the appeal, it will be treated as a request to withdraw the appeal and to reopen prosecution before the examiner, regardless of whether the RCE is proper or improper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Office will withdraw the appeal upon filing of an RCE; applicants should advise the Board when an RCE is filed. If RCE is proper (fee + submission responsive per 1.111) withdraw finality and enter submission; if not fully responsive but bona fide, notify applicant and give time to complete reply (use 7.42.08). If improper (lacks fee/submission), withdraw appeal and treat application per MPEP § 1215.01 (may be abandoned if no allowed claims; pass to issue if claims allowed). Use form paragraph 7.42.06 for proper RCE after appeal.

rubrics_metrics.name: RCE without submission and/or fee after appeal — treatment when no claims allowed
rubrics_metrics.description: If an RCE was filed after appeal and the request lacks the fee and/or the submission required, use form paragraph 7.42.10 to withdraw the appeal and hold the application abandoned if there are no allowed claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner Note: apply this when request lacks fee or submission and there are no allowed claims; reference MPEP § 1215.01.

rubrics_metrics.name: RCE without submission and/or fee after appeal — treatment when claim(s) allowed
rubrics_metrics.description: If RCE filed after appeal includes fee but lacks the required submission, withdraw appeal and pass the application to issue on allowed claim(s). If formal matters are outstanding, give applicant a shortened statutory period of two months to correct them (form paragraphs 7.42.11 - 7.42.14 as appropriate).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Claims indicated as containing allowable subject matter but dependent upon rejected claims are to be considered as if rejected and should be canceled along with rejected claims. Use appropriate form paragraph depending on whether fee or submission is missing and whether formal matters remain.

rubrics_metrics.name: RCE filed after Board decision but before further appeal or civil action — timing and effect
rubrics_metrics.description: Filing of an RCE (accompanied by the fee and a submission) after a decision by the Patent Trial and Appeal Board, but before the filing of a Notice of Appeal to the Federal Circuit or commencement of a civil action, will result in the finality of the rejection or action being withdrawn and the submission being considered, provided timely filed (generally within sixty‑three (63) days).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A Board decision has res judicata effect and is 'law of the case' — a submission containing arguments without either amendment of rejected claims or a showing of facts will not remove new grounds of rejection affirmed by the Board. Use form paragraph 7.42.07 to notify applicant that the appeal has been withdrawn and prosecution reopened.

rubrics_metrics.name: Improper RCE after Board decision — notice and non-entry of submission
rubrics_metrics.description: If an RCE is filed after a Board decision but lacks the fee and/or submission, the RCE is improper and any time period running was not tolled by the filing of the improper request; use form paragraph 7.42.16 to notify applicant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If time for seeking court review has passed, include the form paragraph with a Notice of Allowability or Notice of Abandonment as appropriate; otherwise use PTOL-90. In general, do not enter a submission filed with an improper RCE unless the amendment obviously places the application in condition for allowance and supervisory patent examiner approves. Examiner should state whether any such submission was entered.

rubrics_metrics.name: After appeal to Federal Circuit or civil action — RCE generally unavailable
rubrics_metrics.description: The procedure set forth in 37 CFR 1.114 is not available in an application after the filing of a Notice of Appeal to the Federal Circuit or commencement of a civil action in federal district court, unless the appeal or civil action is terminated and the application is still pending.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an RCE is filed after court review, bring the application to the attention of the supervisory patent examiner or a quality assurance specialist to determine whether the RCE is proper. Unless the application contains allowed claims (or the court's mandate indicates further Office action), termination of an unsuccessful appeal or civil action results in abandonment. See MPEP § 1216.01.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form usage and Examiner Notes guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Use specific MPEP form paragraphs (e.g., 7.42.05, 7.42.06, 7.42.07, 7.42.08, 7.42.09, 7.42.10 - 7.42.16) to notify applicant of the outcome and next steps depending on whether RCE is proper/improper and the procedural posture (after final, after allowance, on appeal, after Board decision, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner Notes identify bracket content (e.g., insert dates, identify reasons for non-responsiveness, list formal matters) and cross-reference relevant MPEP sections (e.g., § 714.03, § 821.03, § 1214.06, § 1215.01, § 1216.01). Follow guidance on when to enter submissions and when to mail Notice of Improper Request for Continued Examination (Form PTO-2051).

rubrics_metrics.name: Time periods and statutory maximums for shortened reply periods
rubrics_metrics.description: When giving shortened statutory periods (e.g., two months to complete a reply when submission not fully responsive; three months for shortened statutory period in first action final after RCE), note that these shortened periods may be extended under 37 CFR 1.136(a) but in no case can any extension carry the date for reply beyond the maximum period of six months set by statute (35 U.S.C. 133).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a first reply is filed within two months and advisory action is delayed, the shortened statutory period may expire on mailing date of advisory action but never later than six months from mailing date of final action. For formal matters outstanding when passing to issue, applicant is required to correct within a two-month shortened statutory period.
